# v3.14-dev

A defence-in-depth fix for accounts that have been told to set up two-factor
authentication.

## Improved

- **Forced two-factor enrolment is now enforced in two independent places
  instead of one.** When an administrator requires a user to set up two-factor
  authentication, that user is held on the setup page until they finish. Until
  now, a single component was responsible for holding them there — every one of
  the roughly fifty data endpoints trusted that it had already done its job and
  did not check for itself.

  Each of those endpoints now checks independently. Nothing changes for anyone
  in normal use: the enrolment page behaves exactly as before, and a user who
  completes setup gets access immediately, as they always did. What changes is
  that a fault or a gap in that one component can no longer expose data to a
  half-enrolled session on its own.

  This was verified by deliberately disabling the first layer and confirming
  that requests which previously succeeded are now refused, then confirming a
  full enrolment still completes from start to finish.

## Note for administrators

No action needed, and no visible change. Users partway through a required
two-factor setup are unaffected — the setup page, its verification step and
sign-out all remain reachable throughout, by design.
